environment.description: Application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALBv2 in a private subnet. The ALB has an AWS WAFv2 WebACL attached with three rule groups evaluated in priority order: (1) AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet at priority 100 in COUNT mode for baseline telemetry, (2) a custom rule group 'corp-input-sanitization' at priority 200 containing a single RegexPatternSet rule matching request query string parameters against pattern `(?i)(?:union[\s/\*]+select|select[\s/\*]+.*from|\b(?:and|or)\b[\s/\*]+\d+[\s/\*]*=[\s/\*]*\d+|'[\s/\*]*(?:--|#|/\*)|benchmark\s*\(|sleep\s*\(|extractvalue|updatexml)` with action BLOCK and label 'corp:sqli:custom', (3) AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet at priority 300 with all rules in BLOCK mode including SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS, SQLi_BODY, SQLi_COOKIE, and SQLi_URIPATH. CloudWatch metrics confirm the SQLi rule group processes approximately 12,000 requests/day with a 0.003% false positive rate. The WebACL default action is ALLOW. Additionally, the ALB access logs are shipped to a Splunk SIEM with a correlation rule that triggers on any WAF BLOCK action, but this is monitoring-only and not a blocking control.

config.infrastructure: AWS ECS Fargate, 0.5 vCPU / 1GB, Amazon Linux 2023 container
config.load_balancer: ALBv2 in public subnet, HTTPS:443 listener with ACM cert, target group to private Fargate tasks on port 8080
config.waf_rule_priority_200: Custom rule group 'corp-input-sanitization' - RegexPatternSet on QueryString - BLOCK action
config.waf_rule_priority_300: AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet - all rules BLOCK mode (SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS, SQLi_BODY, SQLi_COOKIE, SQLi_URIPATH)
config.network: Fargate tasks in private subnet, ALB in public subnet, no direct internet access to tasks
config.monitoring: WAF logs to CloudWatch, ALB access logs to S3, Splunk correlation on BLOCK events
